title: Architectural decision: move RFC 8621 mail-specific SetErrorType variants out of foundation
description:
Background: bd:JMAP-wlip.19 closed the documentation half — the SetErrorType doc now honestly acknowledges that the foundation carries 13 RFC 8621 mail-specific variants alongside the 10 RFC 8620 base variants, while explicitly forbidding further extension variants there. The actual reshape requires a workspace-architectural decision.

Current state (foundation jmap-server::SetErrorType variants):
- RFC 8620 §5.3 base (10): Forbidden, OverQuota, TooLarge, RateLimit, NotFound, InvalidPatch, WillDestroy, InvalidProperties, Singleton, AlreadyExists
- RFC 8621 mail-specific (13): MailboxHasChild, MailboxHasEmail, TooManyKeywords, TooManyMailboxes, BlobNotFound, ForbiddenFrom, InvalidEmail, TooManyRecipients, NoRecipients, InvalidRecipients, ForbiddenMailFrom, ForbiddenToSend, CannotUnsend
- Custom(String) for everything else

Proposal: move the 13 mail variants to a new MailSetErrorType enum in jmap-mail-types and have jmap-mail-server map those to SetErrorType::Custom on the wire. The foundation SetErrorType keeps only the 10 RFC 8620 §5.3 variants plus Custom.

Cost:
- Breaking change to jmap-server (variant removal) — workspace-wide major bump.
- Cascading propagation: every *-server crate that pattern-matches on these variants needs to rebase onto the new shape.
- Every *-server crate's tests that compare SetErrorType::TooManyRecipients need to compare against SetErrorType::custom('tooManyRecipients') instead.
- Public API surface shrinks for the foundation crate (good) but mail-extension callers lose typed pattern-matching (bad).

Workaround if not done: callers of mail-extension errors continue to enjoy typed pattern-matching while callers of other extensions use Custom. The asymmetry is documented but persists.

Decision needed from Mark:
- (a) Schedule the reshape for the next planned workspace major bump.
- (b) Defer indefinitely; keep the asymmetry and the documented carve-out.
- (c) Reshape now (major bump now).

This is closer to (a) territory — the asymmetry is a known cost of the kit-of-parts architecture, and the reshape is well-defined when a major bump arrives anyway.
notes: Decided 2026-10-21 in JMAP-wf92.5 (commit 604bd725): the 13 RFC 8621 mail variants STAY as known typed variants of the shared SetErrorType, which now lives in jmap-types (jmap-server re-exports it) with Other(String) replacing Custom(String). This is the recommended answer in the wf92.5 bead text. Reason: SetErrorType is now shared by servers and clients, so mail servers and mail clients keep one typed match; moving them to a MailSetErrorType would drop typed matching on both sides and only relocate the asymmetry. The variant policy doc still forbids adding further extension-specific variants; other extensions use SetErrorType::from("...") -> Other. No MailSetErrorType reshape.
